reasons: intent_insensitive: question four is no: a different enemy intent would not have changed the line, so the intent is not part of the decision

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: The entire hand. Powder Pop first: it costs 0 energy, places a 5-damage Bomb on the Sludge Spinner, and banks a Spark, taking me from 4 Sparks to 5. Then Firework Finale for 18 (Sparks 5 to 2), then Fwoosh! for 8 (Sparks 2 to 1). That is 26 damage now plus a 5-damage Bomb pending, putting the Spinner from 39 to 13 before the Bomb resolves. All three of those cost 0 energy, so my whole 3 Energy was still free and I spent 1 of it on Duck and Cover for 5 Block against the telegraphed 8, taking 3 instead of 8 and ending at 39/62. Nothing in the hand had to be cut — the hand is entirely affordable, so the only real decision was sequencing.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: Two things. First, the ordering question: with 4 Sparks I can already pay Firework Finale (3) and Fwoosh! (1) exactly, so Powder Pop's Spark is not strictly needed — but leading with it costs nothing and leaves me at 1 Spark instead of 0, so leading was free upside and I took it. Second, and more seriously, holding Firework Finale. It Exhausts, so it is a one-use card, and 18 damage does not kill a 39 HP enemy this turn either way; I considered banking it (and the 3 Sparks) for a turn where it finishes the fight or lands on something bigger. I rejected that because the Spinner is the only enemy on the board, damage now is damage that shortens the number of 8-damage attacks I eat, and holding a card I cannot guarantee redrawing next turn is a worse bet than spending it into the only target.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: It burns Firework Finale permanently — it Exhausts, so there is no later turn where I get that 18 back — and it drains the Spark bank from 4 down to 1, so next turn I start near-empty and Spark-priced cards will mostly be unpayable until Powder Pop-style generation refills me. It also spends the Bomb's Burst +5 on a target I did not set up further, and leaves 2 Energy unused because nothing in hand could absorb it.
answers.q4_different_intent: No. Every card in the hand is affordable simultaneously — three at 0 energy and one at 1 of my 3 — so there is no card the intent could talk me out of playing. A bigger telegraphed attack would not change the line because Duck and Cover's 5 Block is already the only defense available and I am already playing it. A defensive or buffing intent would make that 5 Block worthless, but I would still play it, since holding it gains me nothing that carries to next turn. The most an intent could move is the ordering, and Powder Pop-first is already correct regardless.
